title: CREPE: Controlling diffusion with REPlica Exchange
claim: Our sampler's trajectory starts off-prompt and, after a burn-in period, steadily yields diverse samples that satisfy the new constraint.
layout: 4 rows of image strips, left-to-right, bottom arrow marks iteration
description: Four horizontal strips of small generated images, stacked vertically. Each strip has a bold-and-italic label above it giving a class condition and a text prompt: balloon with 'a blue balloon', pinwheel with 'a colorful pinwheel', Christmas stocking with 'a green Christmas stocking', and cab with 'a yellow cab with dark background'. Each strip holds about 24 thumbnails in sequence. Early images on the left mostly show the generic class: balloons in various colors, red stockings, blue or other-colored cabs. Images further right match the prompt more closely: blue balloons, green stockings, yellow cabs on dark backgrounds. Diversity in pose and composition persists. A long black arrow along the bottom, labeled 'CREPE iteration', shows the order. The eye goes first to the saturated photo thumbnails, then to the labels.
caption: Trajectory of images generated using CREPE for prompted reward-tilting on ImageNet-512, thinned every 8 iterations. After burn-in, the samples align closely with the prompt.
abstract: Inference-time control of diffusion models aims to steer model outputs to satisfy new constraints without retraining. Previous approaches have mostly relied on heuristic guidance or have been coupled with Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) for bias correction. In this paper, we propose a flexible alternative based on replica exchange, an algorithm designed initially for sampling problems. We refer to this method as CREPE (Controlling with REPlica Exchange). Unlike SMC, CREPE: (1) generates particles sequentially, (2) maintains high diversity in the generated samples after a burn-in period, and (3) enables online refinement or early termination. We demonstrate its versatility across various tasks, including temperature annealing, reward-tilting, model composition and classifier-free guidance debiasing, with competitive performance compared to prior SMC methods.
